newsitem.title: UK: Glaxo makes US political donations - paper.
newsitem.headline: Glaxo makes US political donations - paper.

text.p: British drugs firm Glaxo Wellcome faces criticism for giving $500,000 to U.S. political parties over two years without revealing this in its results, said a report in Tuesday's edition of The Times newspaper.
The paper said corporate governance consultancy the Pensions and Investment Research Consultants (PIRC) had discovered from Glaxo that it made political donations though its U.S. operation.
"After further enquiries by The Times, Glaxo admitted the figure for the two years to December 1996 was 'approximately' $500,000," the report said, adding that most was given to the Republican Party.
The paper said PIRC was recommending that shareholders should vote against approving Glaxo's report and accounts over the issue.

"We consider such an expenditure should be approved by the shareholders in advance via a resolution stating the amount, beneficiary and reasons for expenditure," PIRC director Anne Simpson was quoted as saying.
The Times quoted Glaxo as saying the payments were a normal part of business in the U.S. and insignificant relative to the group's U.S. profits.

But it said other representatives of institutional investors were agreed that companies should disclose all political donations, including the Association of British Insurers and the National Association of Pension Funds.
